concepts.title: The cohomology zoo and the realization problem
concepts.blurb: Betti, de Rham, ℓ-adic, and crystalline cohomology take values in different categories yet share parallel Künneth, Poincaré-duality, and Lefschetz formulas. Grothendieck's vision: a universal h: SmProj/k → Mot(k) through which every realization factors.

concepts.title: Correspondences as morphisms
concepts.blurb: Morphisms in Mot(k) are elements of CH*(X×Y) ⊗ Q — algebraic cycles modulo rational equivalence — composed via pushforward/pullback on the triple product. Graphs of morphisms embed varieties; the diagonal acts as identity.

concepts.title: Pure Chow motives
concepts.blurb: Objects (X, p, n) with p an idempotent correspondence and n a Tate twist; morphisms compatible correspondences. Pseudo-abelian envelope of varieties + correspondences, then formally invert the Lefschetz motive. Three flavors — Chow, homological, numerical — by equivalence relation.

concepts.title: The Tate twist Q(n)
concepts.blurb: Q(1) = inverse of the Lefschetz motive h^2(P^1). Realizes as 2πi·Q (Betti, weight −2), shifted Hodge filtration (de Rham), the cyclotomic character (ℓ-adic), Frobenius=1/p (crystalline). Periods include (2πi)^n; mixed Tate motives over Z control multiple zeta values.

concepts.title: Tannakian categories — representations of an invisible group
concepts.blurb: A neutral Tannakian category T over k is k-linear rigid abelian symmetric monoidal with a faithful exact tensor fiber functor ω: T → Vect_k, such that T ≃ Rep_k(Aut⊗(ω)). Solving the category = solving the group.

concepts.title: The motivic Galois group
concepts.blurb: Jannsen (1992) — unconditional. Modulo the standard conjectures, numerical motives are Tannakian with fundamental group G_mot(k) = Aut⊗(ω_B). Realizations recover Gal(Q̄/Q) (étale), Mumford-Tate (Hodge), and a Frobenius scheme (crystalline) as quotients.

concepts.title: Realizations: how Betti, de Rham, ℓ-adic, crystalline all come from one motive
concepts.blurb: Each cohomology theory is a tensor functor R: Mot(k) → C_R. Comparison isomorphisms tie them: Grothendieck (Betti↔dR over C), Artin (Betti↔ℓ-adic), Fontaine (crystalline↔ℓ-adic via B_cris).

concepts.title: The standard conjectures and the road forward
concepts.blurb: Grothendieck (1968): Lefschetz (B), Künneth (C), Hodge (I). Open in general since 1968; modulo (B)+(C) homological = numerical and Mot_hom is Tannakian. Unconditional: Jannsen, mixed Hodge (Deligne), mixed Tate over Z (Deligne-Goncharov-Brown), Voevodsky's DM(k).
